guitar.evidence: Trained knowledge: extremely well documented — SRV's well-worn 1963/1962-hybrid Strat nicknamed "Number One" is among the most famous guitars in blues-rock.

tone.target: Texas blues overdrive with bright Strat bite and vocal sustain
tone.profile: Texas blues overdrive with bright Strat bite and vocal sustain
tone.summary: A classic Texas blues chain using a Boost for initial grit, followed by an OD pedal to push the mids, feeding into a Fender-style amp model with a bright cab and spring reverb.
corrections: Center on SRV-style Texas blues drive
Keep wah as occasional color, not core
Skip delay; keep it mostly dry

rig.name: Stevie Ray Vaughan & Double Trouble - Tightrope - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and background noise.
Provide initial grit and boost the signal into the OD pedal.
Emulate the Tube Screamer-style mid-pushed overdrive essential for Texas blues.
Provide occasional wah color without dominating the tone.
blocks.gap: The C-Wah is a general purpose Wah, suitable for blues use.

blocks.purpose: Bypass or use for subtle saturation if needed (kept inactive as per 'avoid' list).
blocks.gap: No specific distortion module is required; the OD and Amp model handle the core drive.

blocks.purpose: Emulate the Fender combo base and provide clean headroom.
Match the Fender combo sound and provide a bright, articulate tone.
Slightly boost the mids and highs to achieve 'Strat bite' and cut through the mix.
Avoid chorus as per the 'avoid' list.
Provide the small spring reverb characteristic of vintage Fender amps.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism and low-end definition to better capture the punchy Texas blues sound.

proposals.reason: The current US 2x12 may lack the necessary low-end girth and aggressive bite for SRV's style.
proposals.expectedGain: Increased punch and definition in the lower mids/low end.
